audit_findings.title: The retained interest burden is temporarily swap-subsidized
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.32 million annual pre-tax current rate gap; future adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 OE anchor retains interest expense, so any post-swap increase reduces OE; repayment from cash would instead reduce the cash bridge and eliminate the associated interest burden.
audit_findings.evidence: The weighted average interest rate applicable to the HBB Facility and the Prior HBB Facility for the year ended December 31, 2025 was 3.30% (after giving effect to the interest rate swap agreements described below).
audit_findings.explanation: The subsidy is demonstrated: the filed 5.94% stated rate exceeded the 3.30% swap-adjusted effective rate by 2.64 percentage points, equal to approximately $1.32 million on $50 million of borrowings, or 4.4% of the $30.1 million OE anchor. The swaps expire in January 2029, but the future debt balance, refinancing rate, and repayment decision are unknown, so the record cannot establish the valuation adjustment or its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Rerun the DCF from 2029 under explicit refinance and repayment cases; for repayment, reduce bridge cash by the principal funded from cash and remove the corresponding interest expense without double counting.

audit_findings.title: The entire midyear cash balance may not be excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $101.469 million of bridge exposure, equal to $7.54 per share; actual adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Operating cash classified as surplus is added dollar-for-dollar to equity value through the cash and short-term-investment bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We generally use cash on hand or borrowings under our $125 million senior secured floating-rate revolving credit facility (the “HBB Facility”) to finance inventory over the course of the year in anticipation of the fall holiday-selling season.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation adds the entire June 30 cash balance even though the filing says cash finances the seasonal inventory build. The amount exposed equals 19.4% of the $524 million base equity value and is large enough to materially alter the valuation range. This is not a demonstrated $101.469 million error because some or most of the balance may be distributable, particularly after the $36.5 million tariff refund, but the required operating portion has not been established.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a normalized monthly cash and working-capital schedule covering the holiday build, payables, payroll, taxes, restricted foreign liquidity, and the tariff refund; rerun the bridge using only cash above the demonstrated operating minimum.

audit_findings.title: Maintenance capital expenditure may be below the amount embedded in sustainable OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.823 million annual pre-tax depreciation-capex gap, equal to 9.4% of the $30.1 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: If normalized maintenance capital expenditure exceeds the amount deducted in FY2025 OE, the sustainable OE anchor and every forecast cash flow are overstated.
audit_findings.evidence: Depreciation expense from property, plant and equipment, net for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023 was $ 5.6 million, $ 4.5 million, and $ 4.2 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: Filed depreciation of $5.6 million exceeded $2.777 million of property-and-equipment spending by $2.823 million while net PP&E declined. Depreciation is not proof of maintenance requirements, so an error is not demonstrated. Nevertheless, the documented gap is large relative to the anchor and could change the bear-case conclusion if a substantial portion represents deferred replacement spending.
audit_findings.action: Build a maintenance-capex schedule by distribution infrastructure, software, tooling, connected devices, and other PP&E; separate growth projects and rerun all scenarios with the supported recurring maintenance amount.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may capitalize cyclically low compensation expense
audit_findings.mechanism: An abnormally low personnel and incentive-compensation charge inflates FY2025 OE and carries that margin benefit into forecast growth and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The decrease is primarily due to lower personnel costs associated with the restructuring actions taken by management in the second quarter and reduced incentive compensation expense.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that FY2025 SG&A fell $7.440 million partly because of restructuring and reduced incentive compensation, but it does not allocate the decrease between durable savings and temporary accrual reductions. The concern is reinforced by the first-half 2026 SG&A increase of $5.873 million, primarily attributed to higher incentive-related personnel costs, although that period also included $2.8 million of accelerated ERP depreciation. The recurring compensation correction is therefore unresolved, but reasonably capable of being material relative to $30.1 million of anchor OE.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the FY2025 SG&A bridge separating eliminated positions, incentive accruals, ERP depreciation, and other items; normalize incentive compensation to each scenario's assumed performance and rerun OE.

audit_findings.title: A disclosed one-time tariff cost may have been perpetuated in the latest-actual anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $5.3 million pre-tax, equal to 17.6% of the $30.1 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring cost retained in FY2025 OE lowers the anchor, projected OE, and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Gross profit margin decreased to 25.7% in the current year compared to 26.0% in the prior year primarily due to the flow through of a one-time incremental tariff cost of $5.3 million, which negatively impacted full year margin by 90 basis points.
audit_findings.explanation: The $5.3 million charge is filed and expressly described as one-time, with most arising from the temporary 125% tariff spike. The June 2026 filing further reports invalidation of the IEEPA tariffs and receipt of refunds, supporting nonrecurrence. The charge is large relative to anchor OE, although the precise sustainable OE adjustment remains unresolved because ongoing duties, pricing recovery, sourcing effects, taxes, and the portion refunded are not traced through the OE bridge.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $5.3 million by tariff authority and inventory lot, identify amounts refunded or still recurring, apply the appropriate tax effect, and rerun all scenarios using only the supported nonrecurring adjustment.

audit_findings.title: An accrued environmental claim may be missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.3 million net accrued exposure, or up to $3.3 million including the reasonably possible additional loss; $0.17-$0.25 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: An omitted environmental obligation overstates the equity bridge because future settlement consumes cash without necessarily reducing future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, the Company had accrued undiscounted obligations of $ 2.9 million and $ 3.9 million respectively, for environmental investigation and remediation activities.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed $2.9 million accrual less the $0.6 million reimbursement asset gives $2.3 million of net accrued exposure; including the disclosed additional loss of up to $1.0 million gives a $3.3 million upper exposure. That equals approximately 0.4%-0.6% of the $524 million base equity value and $0.17-$0.25 per diluted share, too small to change the stated valuation conclusion. The latest 10-Q also says management considers the obligations immaterial.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether the bridge already includes the net liability; if omitted, deduct the $2.3 million net accrued amount and present the additional $1.0 million as sensitivity.
